title: Learning Dynamic Evidence Routes for Vision Transformer Probing
claim: Different frozen pretrained backbones induce distinct, spatially organized evidence routes over the same input, revealing differences in how they order information.
layout: 5 panels in a row, input then four overlays, shared colorbar below
description: A single horizontal strip. On the far left is the original input photo, a close-up of a seabird with a tan head and long pinkish bill against blue water. To its right are four square panels titled MAE, BEiT, ViT, and DINOv2. Each shows the same bird image overlaid with a coarse patch grid colored by a magma colormap, with dark purple for patches placed early in the learned route and bright cream or yellow for patches placed late. MAE and ViT show large bright blocks on the bird's head and neck, while the background is dark. BEiT is similar but noisier. DINOv2 looks different, with a darker head and scattered light patches elsewhere. A horizontal colorbar below is labeled Earlier to Later, with the caption Expected route position. The eye goes first to the bright bird-head regions.
caption: Patch evidence routes. The same CUB image is shown alongside the SSMProbe route for four frozen backbones. Color encodes each source patch's normalized expected position in the learned sequence, from earlier (dark) to later (bright). Each overlay uses its backbone's image preprocessing and patch grid. Spatial compactness and bird-foreground alignment are measured by pairwise patch distances and official-mask coverage, respectively.
abstract: Probing frozen vision transformers typically uses permutation-invariant aggregation (GAP or $\texttt{[CLS]}$), treating patch tokens as an unstructured set. Content-dependent probes such as self-attention are useful accuracy controls, but they do not expose a fixed token schedule or fixed position weights for auditing. We introduce SSMProbe, a probe of frozen vision transformers that learns a Sinkhorn patch route and reads it with a diagonal S4 decoder. The decoder's causal linear time-invariant (LTI) recurrence yields fixed position coefficients, exposing how patch arrangement interacts with sequential weighting. Held-out spatial predictability measures route organization beyond a location-bias null. On CUB and Cars, MAE, BEiT, DINOv2, and supervised ViT yield spatially organized routes with distinct readout profiles: DINOv2 is $\texttt{[CLS]}$-dominant, while MAE benefits from learned routing over fixed scans. On MAE/ImageNet, Sinkhorn reaches 70.33% accuracy, 5.55 percentage points above the strongest fixed scan.
